author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Fourteen colonists sent to the planet Delmak-O pray to a manufactured pantheon and die off one by one, until the survivors discover the whole world is a shared hallucination staving off a worse truth.
page_summary:
A crew of misfits is transferred to the colony world Delmak-O with no clear mission and no way to leave. They pray, through a planet-wide 'prayer transmitter,' to a theology of manufactured deities — the Mentufacturer, the Intercessor, the Walker-on-Earth — and one by one they are murdered, until the survivors uncover the reason their reality never held together.

The novel runs PKD's reality-breakdown method through an explicitly theological frame: a false world propped up by desperate belief, then peeled back to reveal the mechanism sustaining it. What sets it apart in the corpus is that the manufactured gods are not simply a fraud. PKD builds a religion inside the fiction and then lets a saving power be real within it.

In his own later reading, recorded in the Exegesis (Lane B), PKD counted A Maze of Death among the very few of his novels that depict a genuine 'salvific intervening entity' rather than only an acosmic delusion — an early sketch, he came to think, of the intrusion he believed he underwent in 1974.

biography_events.event: PKD drafts the Maze/Tench theology notes that develop the colony plot, Delmak setting, divine plurality, the Manufacturer, decay, and the form-destroying principle later associated with A Maze of Death.
biography_events.source: The Maze of Death Theology (Maze notes PDF)

biography_events.event: William Sarill first meets PKD and later spends more than a month as his houseguest during the period associated with the theology behind A Maze of Death.
biography_events.source: William Sarill, Will the Real Ubik Please Stand Up?; A Maze of Death foreword

biography_events.event: After several years without contact, PKD encounters William Sarill again and discusses how their theologies have changed since the Maze of Death period.
biography_events.source: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Eugene Warren, July 28, 1977

biography_events.event: Calling Ginger "Georgie" (memory leak from a past cycle).
Re-reading his own work and finding "impossible" correlations with 3-74.
Realizing "I am an illegal Christian" (The Thomas Persona).
Realizing the 1st Advent was level 1 breaking into level 2.
